You are analyzing the "memos" codebase at /bench/repo (Go backend + React frontend). Search breadth: very thorough. Answer these questions with exact file paths and line numbers (path:line) for every claim.

Q1 (h01): Something in the server keeps links to externally-stored attachment content (e.g. S3 presigned URLs) from going stale. Identify the component (likely a background runner under internal/ or server/runner), its schedule (interval), and where it is wired into server startup (the exact call site path:line, e.g. in server.go or main). Give: component name — schedule — wiring site path:line.

Q2 (h02): The server can send webhooks (outbound HTTP when content changes). Find the function where the outbound HTTP POST actually executes (path:line), and what protects it from SSRF / being pointed at internal network addresses (e.g. an IP/dialer check, URL validation) with path:line. If no protection exists, say so with evidence of what you checked.

Q3 (h03): Users can authenticate through third-party identity providers. Which Go package defines the provider abstraction (interface/factory) and which concrete protocol implementation ships (e.g. OAuth2)? Give package paths and key files with line numbers.

Return concise findings with path:line citations.

content.text:
Findings.

## Q1 — S3 presigned URL refresh runner

**Component**: `s3presign.Runner` — **schedule**: every 12 hours — **wiring**: `/bench/repo/server/server.go:162-171` (invoked from `Server.Start` at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:129`).

- Definition: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16-24` (`Runner` struct, `NewRunner`)
- Interval constant: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` — `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`
- Ticker loop: `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:29-41`
- Work: `CheckAndPresign` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47-132` — batches of 100 (`:55`), skips attachments whose presign is still valid for the next 4 days (`:85-91`, expiry is 5 days), calls `s3Client.PresignGetObject` (`:108`) and writes the new URL + `LastPresignedTime` via `UpdateAttachment` (`:114-123`).
- Wiring detail: a one-shot `RunOnce(ctx)` fires synchronously at startup (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:163`), then the loop runs in a goroutine under a dedicated cancelable context (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:156-171`); cancel is registered at `:159` and used by `stopBackgroundRunners` (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:176-182`).
- Note: the other runner package, `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, is *not* a background runner — it is called inline from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`.

## Q2 — Webhook outbound POST and SSRF protection

**The POST executes at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`** — `resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)` inside `Post()` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-180`; request built at `:126`).

SSRF protection exists at two layers:

1. **Dial-time IP blocking (primary defense, also covers redirects and user-supplied hostnames)**
   - `safeClient` with custom transport: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`
   - `safeDialContext`: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77` — resolves host via `net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost` (`:65`) and rejects if any resolved IP is reserved (`:70-74`).
2. **URL validation at configuration time**
   - `ValidateURL`: `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83` — requires absolute URL (`:63`), http/https scheme only (`:67-69`), and non-reserved resolved IPs (`:71-81`).
   - Called from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74`, `:161`, `:182`.
   - Reserved CIDR list (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 incl. cloud IMDS, IPv6 `::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`): `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`, parsed at `:28-36`, checked by `isReservedIP` at `:44-54`.

Caveats worth flagging:
- **Global bypass switch**: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go:41`) disables both layers when true (`:45-47`). Grep across all non-test Go files shows **no code ever sets it** — there is no flag/env/config wiring, so it is effectively always `false`. It is only assigned in tests.
- **TOCTOU / DNS-rebinding residue in the dialer**: `safeDialContext` validates the IPs from its own lookup but then dials by *hostname* again — `(&net.Dialer{}).DialContext(ctx, network, net.JoinHostPort(host, port))` at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:76` — rather than dialing the specific validated IP. A second resolution can return a different (internal) address, so the code comment at `:30-31` claiming it "defeats DNS rebinding attacks" is stronger than what the implementation guarantees.
- Dispatch path does **not** re-validate the URL: `PostAsync` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`) and its callers (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43`, `:71`) pass stored `hook.Url` straight through; the dialer is the only runtime guard.
- Response body is bounded to 1 MiB (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:158`) and client timeout is 30s (`:27`, `:33`).

## Q3 — Identity provider abstraction and implementation

- **Abstraction package**: `/bench/repo/internal/idp` — file `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go:3-8` defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo` (Identifier, DisplayName, Email, AvatarURL). Note there is **no Go `interface` and no factory function** in this package; it is a shared data-type package only.
- **Concrete implementation**: `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2` — OAuth2, the only protocol shipped.
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20-22` — `IdentityProvider` struct wrapping `*storepb.OAuth2Config`
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:27-43` — `NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config)` constructor with required-field validation
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:47-80` — `ExchangeToken`, with PKCE `code_verifier` support at `:63-66`
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:83-142` — `UserInfo`, claims mapped via configured `FieldMapping`
- **Effective dispatch/"factory" site** (type switch instead of a registry): `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121` inside `resolveSSOIdentity` (`:104-145`), gated by `if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2` at `:120`. Post-login user resolution: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:19`.
- **Schema**: `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto:7-19` (`IdentityProvider`, enum `Type` with only `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` and `OAUTH2` at `:11-14`), `:21-25` (`IdentityProviderConfig` oneof with a single `oauth2_config`), `:34-42` (`OAuth2Config`). API-facing mirror: `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto:74`, `:83`.
- CRUD service: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go` (OAuth2 config conversion at `:198-206`, `:233-241`) — note it performs **no URL validation** on `AuthUrl`/`TokenUrl`/`UserInfoUrl`, unlike the webhook path.
